elements.text: SSTables have several advantages:
elements.rawText: SSTables have several advantages:
elements.originalText: SSTables have several advantages:

elements.text:
1. Merging segments is simple and efficient ( merge sort )
2. In order to find a particular key in the file, no longer need to keep an index for all the
keys in memory. Still an index is required to keep an offset of the keys

Maintaining a sorted structure on disk is possible, but maintaining it in memory is much easier.
Data Structures like Red-Black trees or AVL trees.

- When size increase, write to a file ( SSTable file )
- Read from the disk ( memtable ) and if not found read from the disk
- Run compaction time-to-time to discard overwritten or deleted values

elements.text:
Each log-structured storage segment is a sequence of key-value pairs. 
These pairs appear in the order that they were written and values later in the log
take precedence over values for the same key earlier in the log.

We require that the sequence of the key-value pairs is
The format is called Sorted-String Table or SSTable for short.

elements.text:
LSM tree can be slow when looking-up keys that does not exist. 
Looking in the memtable and then all the way back in the segments.



In order to optimise this access, Bloom filter is used.

There are also different strategies to determine the order and timing of how SSTables are compacted and merged.
The most common are size-tiered and leveled compaction.

elements.text: B-TREES
elements.rawText: B-TREES
elements.originalText: B-TREES

elements.text:
- Like SSTables, B-trees keep key-value pairs sorted by key.
- B-trees break the database down into fixed-size block or pages ( 4KB )
- Each page refer to another page but in disk not in memory construct a tree like structure
- The number of references in child pages in one-page of B-tree is called branching factor.

The algorithm ensure that the tree remains balanced. A B-tree with n-keys has a depth of O(log n).
Most databases can fit into a B-tree that is three or four levels deep.

A four level tree of 4 KB pages with branching factor of 500 can store upto 250TB of data.

elements.text:
To handle database resilient to crashes, it is common for B-tree implementations to include an
additional data structure on disk: a write-ahead log ( WAL ) also known as redo log.
This is an append-only file to which every B-tree modification must be written before it can be
applied to the pages of the tree.
